To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Pearl millet lines resistant to ergot, and/or smut, and/or the armyworm have been identified; (2) these lines can be used to develop multiple disease-resistant varieties of pearl millet; (3) the resistance to the armyworm was not correlated with resistance to either ergot or smut; (4) the resistance to smut and to the armyworm is controlled by different genes.
Pearl millet lines ICMP 28, 29, 38, and 600-3 -2-1 showed combined resistance to smut, ergot, and the army worm.
Pearl millet lines ICMPIS 28, ICMPIS 29, ICMPIS 38, and ICMPIS 600-3 2-1 were identified with combined resistance to ergo, smut and armyworm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and utilization of multiple disease resistance in pear millet.
the development of improved pearl millet varieties resistant to ergot, rust, and the army worm.
the evaluation of germplasm and lines for their resistance to ergot and smut and their susceptibility to oriental army worm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pearl millet lines ICMPES-29, ICMPES-38, and ICMPE 600-3 -2 -1 are the first to be identified as having multiple resistance to ergo t, smut, an d oriental armyworm.
the lines identified in the present study are resistant to ergot, and smut, and moderately resistant to oriental army worm, under field conditions.

the pearl millet germplasm is not resistant or immune to ergot, but that some lines show a high degree of resistance or tolerance, which is not expressed as high yields, but as a reduction in yield loss.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of the artificial inoculation/infestation technique in pearl millet breeding is a promising approach to identify and develop multiple disease and insect resistance.
the use of artificial infestation/infection techniques in pearl millet improvement has been successful.
the use of artificial inoculation and infestation in the field can be a useful tool to identify lines with multiple resistance in pearl millet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified lines that have resistance to all 3 of the diseases that are most important to pearl millet production in Asia.
the pearl millet germplasm collection at ICRIS AT is a rich source of resistance to these diseases and pests.
the pearl millet line ICMPES 28 has multiple resistance to smut, ergot, and oriental armyworm.
